new_events.summary: Houthi political bureau member Mohamed al-Bukhaiti told AP that Washington had contacted the Houthis indirectly through Oman after their west-coast advance and that the group had assured the Trump administration it would not target U.S. vessels or other countries' vessels in Bab el-Mandeb, except Saudi-linked targets. He said Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia would continue until Riyadh ended its blockade and that the group remained open to negotiations. Preserve the non-targeting commitment and policy rationale as Houthi claims; the indirect-contact substrate was separately consistent with Trump's public statement that discussions occurred.

existing_event_updates.summary: Reuters/Kpler reported 17 trackable commodity-vessel transits through Hormuz over the weekend, down from 37 the prior weekend and far below the prewar baseline. Sunday showed five tracked exits and two small oil-tanker entries. Reuters explicitly noted that Middle Eastern producers were also moving oil on vessels with transponders off.

Reuters reported Saudi Aramco had increased exports through Hormuz after East-West pipeline disruption. Tanker/satellite data indicated Saudi oil moving through Hormuz averaged about 2.9 million bpd over the previous six days, versus about 700,000 bpd in August, while seven supertankers loaded about 14 million barrels inside the Gulf on Sunday. This is an export-flow adaptation metric, not evidence of normalized commercial traffic.

economic_energy_updates.observed_state: Reuters reported Brent and WTI falling sharply as markets priced hope for U.S.-Iran diplomacy and partial recovery in Saudi exports. Treat the price move as market expectation, not proof of diplomatic progress.
